era_argument: SYNTHETIC: era labels were planted as a different era mixture per segment (synth.ERA_MIXES) and never entered the features. On V4, cluster 2 is the strongest vintage-enriched cluster (lift 3.74, CI [3.59, 3.9]); cluster 1 is the strongest mid-enriched cluster (lift 2.15, CI [2.07, 2.24]); cluster 3 is the strongest modern-enriched cluster (lift 1.58, CI [1.55, 1.61]). Recovering a planted mixture checks the lift and CI code; it is not a claim about how real eras sort into segments.

headline.hero_validation_text: SYNTHETIC: planted k=4 (V1 ARI 0.852); nested gate dAUC -4.29e-05 at signal 0 (null), 0.0265 at 0.9 (passes)

limitations: Synthetic data only: the generator's distributions are design choices (synth.py docstring); nothing here measures the real market.
The planted structure is Gaussian on the log scale with a known k; real markets need not be, which is why the null controls and the weak-separation sensitivity are shown.
No price history is generated, so per-segment trends are not computed.
The in-fold clustering freezes k at the preset's planted k (3) - a mild selection leak, disclosed in Design decisions.
The private licensed-data run and its numbers are not in this repo (see DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-04 — Findings regenerated on synthetic data only).

null_control.methodological_conclusion: mixture criteria respond to non-Gaussian marginals, not only to cluster structure; the gap statistic and bootstrap stability are therefore the structure arbiters, and silhouette/BIC are descriptive.

provenance.label: synthetic
provenance.note: Every number in this report comes from data generated by `cardsegments.synth` (planted segments, planted outcomes), so it shows what the method does when the truth is known. It says nothing about the real market. The private licensed-data run is not published until the price-feed terms are read (see DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-04 — Findings regenerated on synthetic data only).

notes: Realized base rates 0.229 (signal 0) and 0.233 (signal 0.9) against the planted 0.23; the positive liquid class is the minority, so PR-AUC is oriented to it.
The generator removes the gem-rate cluster feature from about 30% of rows (3600 of 12000 at signal 0); they carry the explicit no_cluster category, so the nested comparison runs on the full cohort.
b_log1p_sold_365d equals f_log1p_sales_365 by construction in the generator, so the velocity baseline and that feature column are the same information.
fwd_log_price_change is planted as pure noise on about 20% of rows (2381 eligible at signal 0); its R^2 is a null control, not a finding.

nested_gate.kind: Modelled: pooled out-of-fold ΔAUC of era + velocity + cluster over era + velocity on SYNTHETIC cards, paired group bootstrap; truth is the planted segment effect (0 or 0.9).
nested_gate.lies: Leakage or a gate that always passes would show a lift at signal 0; the signal-0 case must FAIL and the signal-0.9 case must PASS (predictions 8 and 9), and the clusters are re-fit inside every training fold.
nested_gate.question: Does knowing a card's segment help predict whether it sells, beyond era and trailing sales?

null_control.kind: Simulated control: the identical pipeline on a matched-Gaussian sample and on column-shuffled data; truth is 'no structure' by construction.
null_control.lies: Mixture criteria react to non-Gaussian marginals, so BIC/ICL can pick k > 1 on a null; the gap statistic and bootstrap stability are the arbiters, and the gates in tests/test_cluster_gates.py fail if the gap statistic finds structure in a null.
null_control.question: Would the pipeline invent segments in data that has none?

structure.kind: Simulated: gap statistic, silhouette, BIC/ICL and bootstrap ARI on SYNTHETIC cards with planted segments; truth is the planted labels (adjusted Rand index against them).
structure.lies: An easy generator flatters any method; the matched-Gaussian and column-shuffled nulls and the weak-separation sensitivity must read as no structure (tests/test_cluster_gates.py, prediction 4 and 5).
structure.question: Does the selection pipeline find the segments that are really there, and only those?
